concerns.concern: The C = 0 assignment for the Φ ≈ 15° device D3 is weakly supported. Its CNP Landau levels are hard to resolve, and no Hall data are shown along the line where a C = +1 state from ν = −1 would run.
concerns.quote: so the C = 0 assignment rests on Hall data from a device whose fans resolve? In Fig. 4f the CNP Landau levels are hard to make out.

concerns.concern: The devices compared across alignment angle also differ in twist angle (D1 at 0.93°, D3 at 0.83°), and twist angle alone can switch the topology in tDBG. The same-twist comparison (D2 vs D5) is stated but not shown, and twist-angle homogeneity within devices and Landau-level quality are not compared.
concerns.quote: Same-θ devices compared across Φ: no (D2 and D5 stated, not shown); θ homogeneity within a device: no; Landau-level quality compared: no

concerns.concern: The alignment angle Φ appears to be confirmed partly by the measured Chern numbers themselves, which is circular. An independent check of Φ is needed.
concerns.quote: use "the consistency of the measured Chern numbers across all aligned devices" as "a posteriori confirmation of the alignment assignment"

concerns.concern: Unintended hBN–graphene alignment could break C2 symmetry and produce the Chern state. The hBN angles are not reported and no search for hBN-moiré resistive peaks is shown; the issue is only argued in the supplement.
concerns.quote: Report the bottom and top hBN angles from optical edges, and scan density past ±2×10^12 cm^-2 for extra full-filling peaks

concerns.concern: The C = +1 state could be a field-catalyzed Chern insulator from Hofstadter subbands rather than an intrinsic one. No zero-field anomalous Hall signal or field hysteresis at ν = −1 was looked for.
concerns.quote: Sweep B both ways through zero at ν = −1 in D1 and D2 and look for an anomalous Hall signal or hysteresis

concerns.concern: It is unclear whether Rxy is antisymmetrized in field. It is also unclear how the longitudinal admixture masked near CNP in Fig. 4b affects the ν = −1 trajectory where the 97.6% value is read.
concerns.quote: Is Rxy in Fig. 4b,d antisymmetrized in field, and how does the "longitudinal admixture" that you mask near CNP in Fig. 4b enter

concerns.concern: The 97.6% quantization may be a best-case value. It is reached at one field and drops to 79.7% at 2 T and 87.5% near 5 T, so Rxy along the line should be shown at other displacement fields and in other devices.
concerns.quote: falls to 79.7% at 2 T and 87.5% near 5 T (Fig. 4d)

concerns.concern: Only two "representative" devices are shown in field. The Landau fans and Rxy of the other Φ ≈ 0° devices (D2, D4) are not shown, and how the shown data were chosen is not explained.
concerns.quote: Show the D2 and D4 fans and Rxy beside Fig. 4a to d, and say what "representative" meant

concerns.concern: The paper does not explain why the fans were taken at D = 0.6 V/nm. It does not say whether fans were measured at other displacement fields or at negative B, or whether the C = +1 line holds across the whole D range where the zero-field peak exists.
concerns.quote: why that D was chosen, and whether fans were taken at other D or at negative B, isn't stated.

concerns.concern: The total number of devices fabricated and measured is not stated, nor how many at each alignment angle showed the effect.
concerns.quote: how many were fabricated, and whether any were set aside, isn't stated.

concerns.concern: It is not stated whether any devices or cooldowns were set aside, for example for contacts, gate leakage or absence of the ν = −1 state, or why.
concerns.quote: Were any devices or cooldowns set aside (for example for contacts, gate leakage, or no ν = −1 state), and why?

concerns.concern: The main text does not describe the processing steps from raw data to figures, such as the masking in Fig. 4b and the Arrhenius fit range.
concerns.quote: the steps for Rxy (field antisymmetrization, the masking in Fig. 4b) and the Arrhenius fit range aren't described in the main text.
